name: Gamul
overview: Gamul was a male Levite who served as the twenty-second chosen priest among the twenty-four priestly courses. He belonged to the line of Ithamar, one of the sons of Aaron, which highlights his role within the Levitical priesthood. His service is specifically noted in the division of priestly duties established in ancient Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Gamul means 'weaned' in Hebrew. This proper name does not appear to have been given directly by God but is recorded in Scripture to identify this priestly figure.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Gamul as a descendant of Ithamar, indicating his lineage within the Levitical priesthood. Beyond this connection, no additional family relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Gamul's significance lies in his role as one of the twenty-four priestly courses established to organize the service of the priests in the temple. Being the twenty-second chosen priest from the line of Ithamar, he represents the continuation of Aaron's priestly line through Ithamar, emphasizing the orderly and divinely appointed structure of Israel's worship. His mention in 1 Chronicles underscores the importance of maintaining the priestly divisions for the proper functioning of temple duties.
